admission.justification: The route design had real forks (extend the code-root routes, add a caller path, build a second viewer) and the choice fixes the only way a report may be read from the dashboard.

alternatives.option: One read-only route addressed by the launcher's execution selection and its recorded request ID, serving only the report file the launch recorded, under the exact product report root, with a launch-derived file name and named refusals for missing, unreadable or outside-root files.
alternatives.reason: The route adds no path input and no listing, so a caller cannot select a file; the deterministic name keeps a rewritten receipt from substituting a sibling file; the existing notes reader remains the viewer.

alternatives.option: Extend the existing file routes to accept the reports root and take a path from the caller.
alternatives.reason: A caller-selected path is exactly the admission the packet forbids: it would let the dashboard read any file under the root, not only the recorded report.
alternatives.reconsider_when: The product grows a general reports reader with its own confinement and an approved requirement.

alternatives.option: Build a second bespoke report viewer in the dashboard beside the notes reader.
alternatives.reason: The packet requires the existing reader; a second viewer duplicates the display path and its confinement work.
alternatives.reconsider_when: A later requirement needs a report-specific display contract.

consequences: The route serves every launchable role, task-bound or taskless, and answers the report's absence in rule 3's line.
A report absent from the root, unreadable, non-regular or recorded outside the root is refused by name.
An absent report-access alias no longer hides a written canonical report; a genuinely retargeted alias keeps a distinct refusal.
context: Removing the printed report path made the report reachable only through Result, and Result needs to open it. The existing readers refuse a role's report: the file routes read code roots only (a request for a canonical report answered HTTP 400 bad-path) and the notes reader admits a task's notes, not the report of a role without a task. The backend had to gain a route or the report would be lost.
decider: The run's architect amended MIK-R75@v1 with rule 4a on the worker's report and the orchestrator's recommendation (2026-10-05); orchestrator ruling OR-R014 sealed the review-round interpretations, and the current report-route suite (54 cases inside the 203-test, 15-module focused run) passes on the candidate.
